segments.text: Ladies and gentlemen, the store of tomorrow,
Take what you like, total freedom of choice.
You think you choose what you buy.
A clerk, a counter, your list, his hands.
Then Clarence Sanders tore the counter out.
A turnstile at the door, one way in, aisles you had to walk.
And the candy, right by the register.
Customers stop shopping when the basket's heavy.
So he puts the basket on wheels.
Attractive models, paid to push his cards.
Smiling down every aisle, shoppers watch them and copy.
Within weeks, every one of his stores pushes.
Same cart, just a bigger hole to fill.
Brands pay for where your eyes land.
The end of the aisle, sold.
The shelf itself is for sale.
Rose, one aisle, everyone facing where they're told.
So you took a cart you didn't need.
You grabbed the pyramid at the end.
You took what was at eye level.
You slowed down with the music.
You picked up candy at the till.
Every step drawn before you walked in.
You can keep pushing the card, or go quiet, watch, learn.
Like, subscribe, and evolve quietly until you're the wolf.

full_text: Ladies and gentlemen, the store of tomorrow, built around you. Take what you like, total freedom of choice. Freedom, lovely. May I? Sure, one quick word. You think you choose what you buy. Before 1916, you didn't shop. You asked. A clerk, a counter, your list, his hands. Then Clarence Sanders tore the counter out. He called it self-service. You were never serving yourself. I think that's enough. Let me continue, please. A turnstile at the door, one way in, aisles you had to walk. And the candy, right by the register. Theft went up. It didn't matter. Impulse buys paid for it. 1937, Sylvan Goldman sees a problem. Customers stop shopping when the basket's heavy. So he puts the basket on wheels. Nobody touches it. So Goldman hires people. Attractive models, paid to push his cards. Pretending to shop. Smiling down every aisle, shoppers watch them and copy. Within weeks, every one of his stores pushes. Nobody chose the cart. They copied the crowd. The cart, 1937. The cart today. Spot the difference. Same cart, just a bigger hole to fill. An empty cart feels unfinished. Now look at the shelves. Eye level, rented. Brands pay for where your eyes land. The end of the aisle, sold. The shelf itself is for sale. And the music, 1982, one study. Slow songs, shoppers walk slower. Sales climb 38%. The music sets your pace. Look around you. Rose, one aisle, everyone facing where they're told. So you took a cart you didn't need. You grabbed the pyramid at the end. You took what was at eye level. You slowed down with the music. You picked up candy at the till. Every step drawn before you walked in. So who did the shopping? You can keep pushing the card, or go quiet, watch, learn. Like, subscribe, and evolve quietly until you're the wolf.
